memberships.evidence_quote: A bent metal bookmark is straightened with pliers and used again. The existing piece is kept.
memberships.reason: Damage condition: the existing bookmark is bent and is straightened, which the definition lists as a repair. Keep condition: the caption states it is used again and the existing piece is kept. Both conditions have affirmative text.

memberships.evidence_quote: A torn canvas satchel is mended with a needle and spare thread so it can carry books again. The same bag is kept.
memberships.reason: Damage condition: the existing satchel is torn and is mended. Keep condition: the caption states the same bag is kept. Spare thread is a repair material, not the making of a new object. Both conditions have affirmative text.

memberships.evidence_quote: A leaking clay jug is sealed and returned to watering plants. The same jug remains in use.
memberships.reason: Damage condition: the existing jug is leaking and is sealed. Keep condition: the caption states the same jug remains in use. Both conditions have affirmative text.

memberships.evidence_quote: A broken desk organizer is put in recycling and a newly purchased organizer is unpacked in its place.
memberships.reason: The damaged organizer is discarded to recycling and replaced by a different, newly purchased organizer. The definition states that discard or replacement by a different object makes the keep condition false. No repair is stated.

memberships.evidence_quote: Paper offcuts are folded into a new tray.
memberships.reason: The caption states that a new object is made from leftover material. The definition states that making a new object, even from leftover material, is not a repair of an existing object. The repair condition is therefore false.

memberships.evidence_quote: A raw wooden blank is shaped with an electric lathe into a new knob.
memberships.reason: The caption states that a new knob is made from a raw blank. The blank is not described as damaged, and making a new object is not a repair of an existing object under the definition. The repair condition is therefore false.

memberships.evidence_quote: A page of knot diagrams is shown. No completed activity or finished object is described.
memberships.reason: The caption affirmatively states its subject (a page of knot diagrams) and states that no completed activity is described. The definition requires the item's own description to state a repair of a damaged object; this description explicitly states it describes no such activity, so the repair condition is false. This is an explicit negative statement, not missing information.

The caption only gives a background colour and a duration and states that the subject is not described. It does not say whether any damaged object is repaired or kept, so under the definition membership is unknown.
